summary: A dynamic pricing rollout recomputed prices at charge time, so quotes and charges disagreed and 6.3% of payments were rejected. A revert was merged but never deployed, leaving the bad code live. Vigil surfaced the reverted commit as the culprit and the incident was resolved by deploying the revert.

timeline.event: Commit 02c238690b (dynamic pricing engine) merged and deployed to checkout.
Revert 8957606ede merged on main; no deploy followed.
PaymentFailures alert fired for checkout (6.3% price mismatch rejections).
Vigil brief posted: 02c238690b flagged at 0.88 confidence, boosted by the merged-but-undeployed revert.
Incident marked resolved after the revert was deployed.

root_cause: Commit 02c238690b routed quote_total through dynamic_price behind the dynamic_pricing flag and recomputed the price at charge time. Under load the two computations produced different totals, and the payment gateway rejected the charge as a price mismatch.
contributing_factors: The revert was merged without a deploy, so main looked healthy while production did not.
The pricing path had no invariant asserting that the charged amount equals the quoted amount.
impact: Roughly 6% of purchase attempts failed for the duration of the incident, against a 1,200 requests/minute checkout baseline.
resolution: Deployed the existing revert 8957606ede; the payment failure rate returned to baseline within minutes.
went_well: The merged revert was treated as evidence, so the culprit ranked first despite being two and a half hours old.
No manual git archaeology was needed to connect the revert to the live deploy.
went_poorly: Merging a revert was mistaken for shipping a fix; nobody checked the deploy pipeline.
Quote and charge totals were computed twice with no cross-check.

action_items.description: Carry the quoted total through to the charge and assert equality before calling the gateway.
Alert when a revert of a deployed commit stays undeployed for more than 15 minutes.
Add a load test that compares quoted and charged totals across concurrent carts.
